title: Finite etale covers lift over a complete Noetherian base: proper case
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ for $n\ge0$. Let $f:Y\to S$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $Y_n=Y\times_SS_n$ [def-pc-base-change], so that $Y_0=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. Then for every finite etale $Y_0$-scheme $V\to Y_0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category] there exist a finite etale $Y$-scheme $U\to Y$ and an isomorphism of $Y_0$-schemes $U\times_YY_0\cong V$. (No henselian hypothesis is assumed: an $I$-adically complete pair is henselian anyway (Stacks, More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALJ), so this is the complete Noetherian case of the essential surjectivity of $\mathsf{FEt}(Y)\to\mathsf{FEt}(Y_0)$ over a henselian pair, but the proof does not use it.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2, essential-surjectivity proof, complete Noetherian case

proof.text: (The thickenings $Y_m\subseteq Y_n$.) For $0\le m\le n$ the closed immersion $S_m\to S_n$ is defined by the ideal $I^{m+1}/I^{n+1}$ of $A/I^{n+1}$, whose $(n+1)$-st power is $0$; every prime of $A/I^{n+1}$ contains this nilpotent ideal, so $S_m\to S_n$ is surjective. By transitivity of fibre products $Y_m=Y\times_SS_m\cong Y_n\times_{S_n}S_m$, so $j_{m,n}:Y_m\to Y_n$ is the base change of $S_m\to S_n$ along $Y_n\to S_n$; hence it is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] and surjective [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. Its ideal sheaf is $I^{m+1}\mathcal O_{Y_n}$, whose $(n+1)$-st power is $I^{(m+1)(n+1)}\mathcal O_{Y_n}=0$ as $I^{n+1}\mathcal O_{Y_n}=0$; so $Y_m\subseteq Y_n$ is a finite order thickening [def-sbc-first-order-thickening]. By [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-closed-immersion-universal-homeomorphism] each $j_{m,n}$, in particular $j_{n,n+1}:Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ and $j_{0,n}:Y_0\to Y_n$, is a universal homeomorphism.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2 (label lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair), proof, paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when A is Noetherian and I-adically complete' (same as the complete local case of Lemma 0A48); 'Let X_n = X x_{Spec A} Spec(A/I^{n+1}) ... the inclusions X_0 -> X_1 -> X_2 -> ...'

proof.text: (Lifting $V$ to a compatible system of etale $Y_n$-schemes.) Put $V_0=V$. Given an etale $Y_n$-scheme $V_n$, apply [lemma-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-site-equivalence] to the universal homeomorphism $j_{n,n+1}:Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$ (step 1): base change along $j_{n,n+1}$ is an equivalence from etale $Y_{n+1}$-schemes to etale $Y_n$-schemes, so there are an etale $Y_{n+1}$-scheme $V_{n+1}$ and an isomorphism of $Y_n$-schemes $V_{n+1}\times_{Y_{n+1}}Y_n\cong V_n$. Composing it with the projection gives $V_n\to V_{n+1}$ over $j_{n,n+1}$, and the square formed by $V_n\to V_{n+1}$, $V_n\to Y_n$, $V_{n+1}\to Y_{n+1}$, $j_{n,n+1}$ is cartesian by construction. By induction and transitivity of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product], $V_n\times_{Y_n}Y_0\cong V$ as $Y_0$-schemes for every $n$. (Stacks cites Etale Morphisms, Theorem 039R, for thickenings with the same underlying space, which is the case here; the DAG node is its generalization to universal homeomorphisms, Stacks 04DZ, whose Lean `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.isEquivalence_etale` is sorry-free on slopmaster2.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2 (label lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair), proof, paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when A is Noetherian and I-adically complete' (same as the complete local case of Lemma 0A48); 'By Etale Morphisms, Theorem 039R the inclusions ... induce equivalence of categories between the category of schemes etale over X_0 and the category of schemes etale over X_n'

proof.text: (Each $V_n\to Y_n$ is finite.) By step 1, $Y_0\subseteq Y_n$ is a finite order thickening, and by step 2, $V\cong Y_0\times_{Y_n}V_n$ as $Y_0$-schemes, i.e. $V\to Y_0$ is the base change of $V_n\to Y_n$. Since $V\to Y_0$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-thickening-finite-cartesian] shows that $V_n\to Y_n$ is finite. So $(V_n\to Y_n)_n$ is a system of finite morphisms with cartesian transition squares.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2 (label lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair), proof, paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when A is Noetherian and I-adically complete' (same as the complete local case of Lemma 0A48); 'if U_n -> X_n corresponds to a finite etale morphism U_0 -> X_0, then U_n -> X_n is finite too, for example by More on Morphisms, Lemma 09ZW'

proof.text: ($V$ is proper over $S_0$.) The projection $Y_0\to S_0$ is the base change of the proper morphism $f$ along $S_0\to S$, hence proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. The morphism $V\to Y_0$ is finite, so the composite $V\to Y_0\to S_0$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (c).

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2 (label lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair), proof, paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when A is Noetherian and I-adically complete' (same as the complete local case of Lemma 0A48); 'In this case the morphism U_0 -> Spec(A/I) is proper as X_0 is proper over A/I'

proof.text: (Algebraization.) The proper morphism $f:Y\to S$ is separated and of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-algebraize-finite-over-proper] to $X=Y$ over the complete Noetherian ring $(A,I)$, with $X_n=Y_n$ and the system of finite morphisms $V_n\to Y_n$ with cartesian squares (steps 2, 3), the hypothesis that $V_0=V$ is proper over $S_0$ being step 4. It gives a finite morphism $g:U\to Y$ together with isomorphisms of $Y_n$-schemes $U\times_YY_n\cong V_n$ compatible with the transition maps, and $U$ is proper over $S$. In particular $U_0:=U\times_YY_0\cong V$ as $Y_0$-schemes. (Stacks' index $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^n)$, $n\ge1$, is ours shifted by one.)

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2 (label lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair), proof, paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when A is Noetherian and I-adically complete' (same as the complete local case of Lemma 0A48); 'Thus we may apply Grothendieck's algebraization theorem (in the form of Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09ZT) to see that there is a finite morphism U -> X whose restriction to X_0 recovers U_0'

proof.text: ($g$ is etale along $U_0$.) $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ Noetherian is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], and $f$ is of finite type, so $Y$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. The finite morphism $g$ is of finite type: it is affine, hence quasi-compact, and over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ with $B$ a finite $R$-module, hence a finitely generated $R$-algebra [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $Z=Y_0\subseteq Y$, the closed subscheme with ideal sheaf $\mathcal J=I\mathcal O_Y$ (step 1). Its $n$-th infinitesimal neighbourhood is cut out by $\mathcal J^{n+1}=I^{n+1}\mathcal O_Y$ [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], i.e. it is $Y_n$, and $Y_n\times_YU\cong V_n$ is etale over $Y_n$ for all $n$ (steps 2 and 5). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-infinitesimal-neighbourhoods] there is an open subscheme $W\subseteq U$ containing $g^{-1}(Y_0)$ with $g|_W:W\to Y$ etale.

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2 (label lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair), proof, paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when A is Noetherian and I-adically complete' (same as the complete local case of Lemma 0A48); 'By More on Morphisms, Lemma 0A43 we see that U -> X is etale at every point of U_0'

proof.text: ($W=U$.) Let $u\in U$ and let $T=\overline{\{u\}}$, a nonempty closed subset of $U$. The structure morphism $h=f\circ g:U\to S$ is proper (step 5), hence universally closed and in particular a closed map (base change along $\mathrm{id}_S$) [def-weil-proper-morphism]; so $h(T)$ is a nonempty closed subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical] it contains a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq I$; pick $t\in T$ with $h(t)=\mathfrak m\in V(I)$. The underlying set of $Y_0=Y\times_S\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ is $f^{-1}(V(I))$: over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq Y$ it is $\operatorname{Spec}(R/IR)$, whose points are the primes of $R$ containing $IR$, i.e. lying over $V(I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Hence $g(t)\in Y_0$, so $t\in g^{-1}(Y_0)\subseteq W$ (step 6). Since $t\in\overline{\{u\}}$ and $W$ is an open neighbourhood of $t$, $W$ meets $\{u\}$, i.e. $u\in W$. Thus $W=U$ and $g:U\to Y$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Fundamental Groups, Lemma 0GS2 (label lemma-finite-etale-on-proper-over-henselian-pair), proof, paragraph 'Essential surjectivity when A is Noetherian and I-adically complete' (same as the complete local case of Lemma 0A48); 'However, since every point of U specializes to a point of U_0 (as U is proper over A), we conclude that U -> X is etale' (written out: closed image of a proper morphism, and I in the Jacobson radical of A by Algebra, Lemma 05GI)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $g:U\to Y$ is finite (step 5) and etale (step 7), so $U$ is a finite etale $Y$-scheme [def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], and step 5 gives the isomorphism of $Y_0$-schemes $U\times_YY_0\cong V_0=V$.
